messages.subject: Repeated measures, unbalanced, fixed and random factors? Within vs within_full? Covariance structure?
parts:
Hi all,

I don’t usually analyse repeated measures and would be grateful if someone with an experienced eye could have a look at my use of ezANOVA and let me know if I’ve don’t it correctly please.

My experiment compares two methods of measuring fish (Fixed factor: method N, method S). I have people (Random: subject) who are randomly assigned to one of the methods. I have a 5 fish, which each subject measures one after the other (that’s my repeated measure, fish within subject). The data (dv) I am using is the relative difference between the measured length (ML) and the true length (TL) i.e. (ML-TL)/TL which is generally small and always positive or zero e.g. 0.0223 ( I am using this relative difference or % error rather than comparing lengths because my hypothesis is all about accuracy which people relate to as a % error).  My data are unbalanced (Method S has 16 subjects and Method N has 30 subjects) so I have set type =2.  

I have used ezDesign to identify missing cells and removed those subjects from the dataset. My scipt is :

myanova = ezANOVA(

  data = data

  , dv = abs_percent_diff

  , wid = subject

  , within = .(fish)

  , between = .(method)

  , type = 2

)

 

print(myanova)

 

the output is

Warning: Data is unbalanced (unequal N per group). Make sure you specified a well-considered value for the type argument to ezANOVA().

>

> print(myanova)

$ANOVA

4 method:fish   4 176 3.263954 1.303306e-02     * 0.04711769

4 method:fish 0.7129335 0.1105804     

 

$`Sphericity Corrections`

3        fish 0.85519 1.006421e-05         * 0.9360341 4.420525e-06         *

4 method:fish 0.85519 1.832917e-02         * 0.9360341 1.514544e-02         *

 

My specific questions are,

1)      should / can I use within or within_full. I don’t get a sphericity test when using within_full nor a test of the interaction method:fish.

2)      There seems to be no option here to define a covariance structure such as compound symmetry. Is there some sort of default setting or is this not applicable in my case?

messages.subject: Re: [ez4r] Repeated measures, unbalanced, fixed and random factors? Within vs within_full? Covariance structure?
parts: First, sorry for missing your message sent last night; the mailing list has a spam-prevention measure such that users' first messages have to be approved by a moderator before they are posted to the list, and while I was notified immediately of this second message, something about the first message marked it as spam so I wasn't notified that it was waiting to be approved. Let me know if there are any questions from that initial message that you need answered. Otherwise, to address this message:

On Wed, Nov 5, 2014 at 6:16 PM, James W <james...@talkingnature.com> wrote:

1)      should / can I use within or within_full. I don’t get a sphericity test when using within_full nor a test of the interaction method:fish.

Use "within" as you have in the code you included in your message. "within_full" really shouldn't be a user-visible option to ezANOVA; it's there because ezPlot and ezStats call ezANOVA internally, and there are some rare circumstances where you might need the "within_full" argument when calling those functions. There should never be need to use the "within_full" argument when calling ezANOVA alone. (FYI, the rare circumstance under which you'd want the "within_full" argument is when using ezPlot or ezStats to plot/tabulate a main effect or interaction involving one or more within-Ss variables when there are additional within-Ss variables over which you want to collapse *AND* your data aren't already collapsed to cell means. In this case you need to use within_full to tell ezPlot/ezStats the full within-Ss design, which in turn pass this on to ezANOVA, which is the function that does the automatic-collapsing-to-cell-means and computation of FLSDs).
2)      There seems to be no option here to define a covariance structure such as compound symmetry. Is there some sort of default setting or is this not applicable in my case?

Nope. Repeated measures ANOVA assumes sphericity, which is a less strict requirement than compound symmetry. I'm not familiar with tools other than bayesian approaches like that provided by rstan (http://mc-stan.org) that permit specification of the covariance structure.

Finally, you might consider looking at mixed effects modelling for this data as it would let you specify participants and fish as crossed random effects, possibly giving you increased power for your inference on your "method" variable. See the lme4 package or the ezMixed function. (or, rstan if you feel up to coding the mixed effects model in a bayesian context)
